items.label: VexLife Local VoiceInput
items.purpose: Deliver reliable browser-independent local dictation in VexLife: microphone audio remains local, VexLife owns speech-to-text realization instead of depending on browser Web Speech, transcript enters the exact existing Composer, existing Send remains the only Conversation commit, and the capability has explicit provider/runtime/currentness/privacy/recovery/lived proof.

items.label: Preserve and finish the existing VoiceInput product surface
items.purpose: Carry forward the current VexLife-Prod #231 VoiceInput Family, microphone control, permission/capture, waveform, Composer projection, Stop behavior and VexLogger evidence as the Product-side baseline, while removing browser SpeechRecognition from its role as the final ASR provider only when the local ASR path is ready.

items.label: Select and qualify the local ASR provider
items.purpose: Evaluate runnable local speech-to-text candidates on the current Apple-silicon VexLife product path and select only after evidence covers local-only custody, license/distribution viability, model size/acquisition, dependency/runtime footprint, supported audio format, English baseline accuracy, usable latency, partial/final transcript behavior, Stop/cancellation, language expansion, failure observability and version/currentness qualification.

items.label: Define the local audio-ingress and transcription contract
items.purpose: Define the smallest VexLife-owned loopback boundary that accepts the current presentation's microphone audio and returns bounded transcription observations without creating a second Conversation, transcript store, browser-specific semantic branch, Vex Perception coupling or unnecessary raw-audio persistence.

items.label: Realize and qualify the local ASR runtime
items.purpose: Materialize the selected local ASR model/runtime under explicit version, artifact, dependency, health/currentness, cancellation, recovery and cleanup rules, and prove that bounded microphone audio can produce transcript observations locally on the current Mac product path.

items.label: Rebind VoiceInput from browser ASR to local VexLife ASR
items.purpose: Replace browser SpeechRecognition as the dictation provider while preserving the existing VoiceInput Family semantics, browser/native microphone capture boundary, waveform, editable Composer destination, existing Send commit boundary, Stop/cancellation behavior and VexLogger chronology.

items.label: Prove local audio privacy, security and recovery boundaries
items.purpose: Use the existing Vex Security Assurance route selectively to prove the actual local VoiceInput sensitive-data and model/runtime boundaries: microphone authorization, loopback admission, transient audio custody/retention, no cloud transcription, no transcript/audio leakage into VexLogger/Memory/Conversation before Send, model artifact provenance/update, cancellation, cleanup and recovery.

items.label: Prove browser-independent local dictation end to end
items.purpose: On exact current VexLife source, prove representative browser presentations can capture microphone audio and reach the same VexLife-owned local ASR path without depending on each browser's SpeechRecognition backend; prove microphone permission, local transcript, waveform, editable Composer, Stop, retry/recovery, existing Send and debug chronology in lived use.

items.label: Define the Local ASR selection relationship
items.purpose: Define the smallest domain-local semantic selection relationship for choosing among qualified local ASR provider/model coordinates without inventing a generic configuration foundation: preserve selected != installed != current != active-session, reuse VexFamily ownership law only if lawful State + Control + Effect semantics are actually earned, keep provider catalog/currentness outside the selection owner, persist through the rightful Home setting/Store boundary, and keep VoiceInput semantics provider-agnostic.

transitions.reason: Current upstream source review narrowed the first runnable comparison to sherpa-onnx versus whisper.cpp: sherpa-onnx pressures direct Kotlin/JVM streaming integration and cross-platform packaging; whisper.cpp pressures a minimal native Whisper runtime with strong Apple acceleration and broad platform support. MLX Whisper and WhisperKit remain bounded alternatives. Provider selection is still held pending exact Mac qualification and model-license/provenance evidence.
